summary.text: 睡 is a phonosemantic character combining 目, which contributes an eye-related meaning, with 垂 as a sound element. The traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting”; current meanings include “sleep” and “doze.”

formation.text: Phonosemantic: 目 contributes an eye-related meaning, while 垂 supplies the sound. The traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting.”

components.text: 目 means “eye” and contributes an eye-related semantic association in 睡; it does not depict a whole sleeping scene.
垂 is identified as the sound element. In the Baxter–Sagart reconstruction, its form closely matches 睡 before 睡’s extra *-s ending; this supports, but does not prove, the phonetic role.

sound.text: Baxter–Sagart reconstructs 垂 as *[d]o[j] and 睡 as *[d]o[j]-s, a close same-system comparison with an added ending in 睡.
The locally recorded Mandarin readings are chuí for 垂 and shuì for 睡. This modern pair is a reading comparison, not evidence by itself for their historical phonetic relationship.

history.text: The traditional analysis makes 睡 from 目 and 垂. A later commentary connects 目 with drooping eyelids; this is an interpretation of the graph, not proof of its earliest construction.
No verified early inscription or physical image is available here to trace 睡’s graphic evolution. A modern redrawing in seal-script style does not document an ancient artifact.

uncertainties.text: The earliest physical attestation and detailed graphic evolution of 睡 remain unresolved. The transmitted text examples do not establish manuscript dates or a chronology from sleeping while seated to broader sleep and lying down.
The reconstructed sound comparison supports the phonetic analysis but does not prove it by itself. The Mandarin readings come from local data; direct Unihan character pages could not be verified.

senses.text: The traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting.” It provides an early lexical framing, but does not establish manuscript dates or that this was the word’s original meaning.

senses.period: attested in transmitted classical examples; dating unresolved
senses.text: Transmitted text examples use 睡 for sleeping or dozing. The evidence does not establish when this broader use arose relative to the sitting-sleep gloss.

senses.period: Qing example recorded; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: A later example is glossed “lie down.” The evidence does not establish a semantic path from sleeping to lying down.

limitations.text: The evidence records distinct historical and current uses but does not establish a chronological chain among sleeping while seated, broader sleep, and lying down; no semantic-development links are asserted.

overview.text: 睡 combines 目, “eye,” with 垂 as a sound element. Its traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting”; today it means “sleep” or “doze.”

components.text: 目 links 睡 to the eyes, the body part associated with sleep.
垂’s reconstructed sound closely matches 睡 before 睡’s extra *-s ending.

relationships.text: Within 睡, 目 contributes the eye-related semantic association in the traditional analysis.
